extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and examiners involved in claim drafting and prosecution (especially AI/ML, biotech, and chemical fields)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examination criteria for assessing whether a patent description supports and enables claimed subject matter (support/enablement), with examples from AI/ML, biotech, and chemical composition cases. Focuses on when claim generalizations exceed the disclosure and what evidence or amendments may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description sufficiency / enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: The description sets forth the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete to such an extent that a person skilled in the art can carry it out. Description discloses the invention sufficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner looks for a disclosure that permits a skilled person to make and use the invention. Antipatterns: only high-level statements, speculative assertions, or no working examples. If the skilled person cannot reproduce the invention from the description (even with common general technical knowledge), enablement is lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support requirement (Article 36(6)(i)) / claim must be supported by description
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed technical solution must be obtainable from the contents sufficiently disclosed in the description and must not go beyond the scope of the contents disclosed in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that generalize beyond concrete embodiments or facts disclosed in the description (e.g., claiming 'any feature value representing face shape' when only face-outline angle was supported) fail the support requirement. Remedy: narrow or amend claims to the supported embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement (Article 36(4)(i)) / ability to carry out
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must provide a clear and sufficient disclosure so that a person skilled in the art can make and use the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If essential correlations, parameters, or production conditions are missing, or only model estimations (without verification) are given, the invention may be held not enabled. Examiner may require experimental evidence or deletion/narrowing of unsupported claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim scope must not exceed the disclosure (no unsupported generalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of a claim cannot be expanded or generalized beyond the scope of the contents disclosed in the description. Generalizations that contain speculative content or unproven effects are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (i) claiming an estimation model that accepts 'any feature value representing face shape' when only face-outline angle correlation is shown; (ii) claiming allergy incidence estimation for any allergic reaction when only contact dermatitis was supported. Antipattern: asserting broad functional results without specific enabling disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to disclose critical correlations or causal relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claimed invention relies on a correlation (e.g., between image-derived features and body weight, or cell-shape change and allergic reaction incidence), the description must disclose that correlation or provide evidence that a skilled person would reasonably expect it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the correlation was not common general technical knowledge at filing, the applicant must provide experimental data or other disclosure that shows the correlation. Mere statements that 'any feature value may be used' without evidence are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI/ML-specific disclosure: training data and model performance
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions relying on trained AI/ML models, the description should disclose relevant training-data characteristics and performance or verification of the trained model (performance evaluation results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipatterns: describing that a 'trained model predicts X' without (i) specifying the training-data content/structure, (ii) describing how the model was trained, or (iii) showing performance/accuracy/validation. Examiner may treat unverified model estimations as non-substitutive for experimental proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental verification required when claimed effect is empirical
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claimed technical effect depends on empirical results (e.g., curing strength, estimation accuracy), the description should include experiments or verified evidence supporting that effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: relying solely on model-estimated results or speculative statements without any experimental data. Where only estimation results are disclosed, the examiner may find the disclosure insufficient unless estimation accuracy is validated and measurement methods are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of measurement methods and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement methods and conditions for claimed measured outcomes should be specifically disclosed in the description when claims depend on those measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the description specifically disclosed how to measure curing strength within 5 minutes and after 24 hours. Including measurement method/conditions helps enable reproducibility; omission weakens enablement/support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common general technical knowledge must be legitimately applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners will consider common general technical knowledge at the time of filing, but such knowledge cannot be used to fill gaps where the required correlation or technical basis was not in fact common knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the correlation or capability cannot reasonably be presumed from general knowledge at filing, the applicant must provide supporting disclosure. Antipattern: assuming unknown correlations simply because a general concept (e.g., 'models can output data for new inputs') is known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on extrapolating across biological/technical subtypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalizing results across biologically or technically distinct subtypes (e.g., various allergic reactions, different facial features) requires disclosure because mechanisms may vary among types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: experimental support for contact dermatitis does not automatically support claims for other allergic reactions. Applicants should limit claims to supported types or provide broader supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compositions defined by component ranges require support for claimed functional effect
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim defines a composition by component ranges and asserts a functional performance (e.g., curing strength threshold within a time), the description must support that the claimed ranges achieve the asserted effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: presenting a model prediction that a composition within specified ranges would meet the performance target without any experimental verification. The examiner may require actual embodiments or validated model accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution remedy: amend claims to overcome lack of support/enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can overcome a reason for refusal by amending or deleting unsupported claims (e.g., deleting an overbroad independent claim and leaving a supported dependent claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance shown in cases: narrowing claims to embodiments actually disclosed (for example, keep Claim 2 supported by description and delete overbroad Claim 1). Applicants should consider targeted amendments rather than speculative generalizations.
